extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners handling continuation/divisional/CPA filings before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for filing and processing continuation, divisional, continued prosecution (CPA), and related continuing applications (including oath/declaration, power of attorney, entity status, affidavits, extensions, abandonment, and examination issues) under relevant CFR provisions and MPEP guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement requirement for continuing applications (37 CFR 1.63(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A newly executed substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 is not required in a continuing application that claims the benefit of an earlier-filed application (35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c)) provided a substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 was executed by or with respect to such inventor and filed in the earlier-filed application, and a copy of such substitute statement showing the signature or an indication thereon that it was executed is submitted in the continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition for omission of a newly executed substitute statement: the earlier-filed application must already contain a proper substitute statement and the continuing application must submit a copy showing execution/signature. This applies to continuations/divisionals relying on earlier substitute statements; check signature or clear indication of execution on the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA Rule 47 (37 CFR 1.63(d)(3)) - decision accompanying copies of oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the executed oath or declaration submitted as a copy in a continuation/divisional was originally filed in a prior application accorded status under 37 CFR 1.47, the copy must be accompanied by a copy of any decision granting a petition to accord 37 CFR 1.47 status to such application unless all nonsigning inventor(s) or legal representative(s) have filed an oath or declaration to join in an application of which the continuation or divisional claims benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If some nonsigning inventors subsequently join in applications, a copy of any oath/declaration filed by the inventor or legal representative who subsequently joined must also accompany the copy of the executed oath or declaration. This ensures the prior Rule 47 grant is documented and that later joiners' documents are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and notice when continuation contains unsigned oath and Rule 47 decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation/divisional applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) prior to Sept.16, 2012 that contain a copy of an oath/declaration not signed by one of the inventors plus a copy of the decision according 37 CFR 1.47 should be forwarded by OPAP to the Office of Petitions. The Office of Petitions will mail applicant a letter stating that 'Rule 47' status has been accorded to the continuation/divisional application, but will not repeat notice to the nonsigning inventor nor announcement in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the processing channel (OPAP → Office of Petitions) when unsigned oaths are present with a Rule 47 decision. Expect a petitions-office letter acknowledging Rule 47 status; do not expect redundant notices to nonsigning inventors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's oath/declaration content for applications filed on/after Sept.16, 2012 (35 U.S.C. 115)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the filing date of the continuing application is on or after Sept.16, 2012, the inventor's oath or declaration in the continuing application must state that the inventor (1) is an original inventor of the claimed invention; and (2) authorized the filing of the patent application for the claimed invention. The oath/declaration also must contain an acknowledgement that any willful false statement made is punishable under 18 U.S.C. §1001 by fine or imprisonment up to 5 years, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the continuing application claims benefit of a pre-Sept.16,2012 filing, the continuing application's oath/declaration must meet the revised 35 U.S.C.115 content requirements when its filing date is on/after Sept.16,2012. Examiners should ensure these statements and the criminal-statement acknowledgement are present and may require amendment if absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior power of attorney in continuing applications (37 CFR 1.32(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept.16, 2012, a power of attorney from a prior national application for which benefit is claimed may have effect in the continuing application if a copy of the power of attorney from the prior application is filed in the continuing application, unless: (1) the power of attorney was granted by the inventor; and (2) the continuing application names an inventor who was not named in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a copy of the prior power of attorney in the continuing application clarifies who has POA; Office recommends POA be from the assignee where one exists. For apps filed on/after Sept.16,2012, POA may only be signed by the applicant (see 37 CFR 1.42) or patent owner for reissue applications. If the above two exceptions apply, the prior POA will not have effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address identification when using prior application papers (37 CFR 1.33(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where application papers from a prior application are used in a continuing application and the correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, an application data sheet or separate paper identifying the correspondence address to be used for the continuing application must be submitted. Otherwise the Office may not recognize the change of correspondence address effected during prosecution of the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always submit explicit identification of the correspondence address in the continuing application when relying on prior papers that experienced an address change, to avoid misrouting and nonrecognition of the desired address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA requirement to identify changes in power of attorney or correspondence address (37 CFR 1.63(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed prior to Sept.16, 2012, where the power of attorney or correspondence address was changed during prosecution of the prior application, the change in power of attorney or correspondence address must be identified in the continuation or divisional application; otherwise the Office may not recognize the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing continuations/divisionals of pre-AIA applications, explicitly identify any mid-prosecution changes in POA or correspondence address to ensure the continuing file reflects those changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small entity and micro entity status assertions for continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If small entity status has been established in a parent application and is still proper and desired in a continuation/continuation-in-part/divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a new assertion as to continued entitlement to small entity status under 37 CFR 1.27 is required. Refilling under 37 CFR 1.53 as a continuation/divisional/CIP requires a new certification of entitlement to micro entity status in the continuing application (see 37 CFR 1.29(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity status does not automatically carry over; applicants must make fresh assertions/certifications in the continuing application. See MPEP §509.03 (small) and §509.04 (micro).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations filed during prior prosecution do not automatically become part of 37 CFR 1.53(b) continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.130, 1.131, 1.132) filed during prosecution of the prior nonprovisional application do not automatically become part of a continuation or divisional filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b). Where it is desired to rely on an earlier-filed affidavit/declaration, the applicant should make such remarks of record in the 1.53(b) application and include a copy of the original affidavit/declaration filed in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 2.03 (Affidavits or Declarations in Prior Application) to instruct applicant to include remarks of record and a copy of the original affidavit/declaration. Note examiner guidance: do not use that form paragraph for 1.53(d) CPAs, since affidavits/declarations in the parent 1.53(d) may automatically become part of the CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time for establishing continuity must be filed in the prior application as a separate paper
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extension of time is necessary to establish continuity between the prior application and a continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), the petition for an extension of time must be filed as a separate paper directed to the prior nonprovisional application. Under 37 CFR 1.136(a)(3), an authorization to charge all required fees will be treated as a constructive petition for an extension of time in any concurrent or future reply requiring a petition for an extension of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuing application is a new application and not a reply to the last Office action in the prior application; therefore petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.17 for an extension must be filed separately in the prior application and accompanied by a certificate of mailing (37 CFR 1.8) or Priority Mail Express certificate (37 CFR 1.10) if those benefits are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing application is a new application; filing date and records are separate
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuing application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b) is a new application which is assigned a new application number and filing date and is maintained separately from the file of the prior application. The filing of a continuing application is not a paper directed to, or placed in, the file of the prior application and is not a 'reply' to the last Office action in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it is a new application, procedural steps (like petitions for extensions) must be taken in the prior application; do not assume actions in the continuation automatically affect the parent file unless appropriate papers are filed in the parent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment of the prior nonprovisional application (37 CFR 1.138 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.53(b) practice, the prior nonprovisional application is not automatically abandoned upon filing of the continuing application. If the prior nonprovisional application is to be expressly abandoned, such a paper must be signed in accordance with 37 CFR 1.138. A registered patent practitioner not of record acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 may also expressly abandon a prior nonprovisional application as of the filing date granted to a continuing application when filing such a continuing application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit, properly signed express abandonment papers are required to abandon a prior nonprovisional when desired. If the prior application has an allowance or issue fee concerns exist, see 37 CFR 1.313 and MPEP §711.01 regarding withdrawing from issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue requirement when issue fee already paid (37 CFR 1.313)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the prior nonprovisional application which is to be expressly abandoned has a notice of allowance issued therein, the prior nonprovisional application can become abandoned by nonpayment of the issue fee. However, once an issue fee has been paid in the prior application, a petition to withdraw the prior nonprovisional application from issue must be filed before the prior application can be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing matters: if issue fee already paid, file petition under 37 CFR 1.313 (withdrawal from issue) before attempting to abandon; be aware of interplay with continuing-app filing dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligations concerning new matter when relying on prior oath/declaration or preliminary amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a copy of the oath/declaration from a prior application was filed in a continuation/divisional application, if the examiner determines that new matter is present relative to the prior application, the examiner should so notify the applicant in the next Office action (preferably the first Office action) and require applicant to delete the benefit claim or redesignate the application as a continuation-in-part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary amendments present on filing date are part of the original disclosure; amendments must comply with 37 CFR 1.121. The Office may require a substitute specification for preliminary amendments. If new matter is present in preliminary amendments, examiner should follow MPEP §§211, 608.04(b), and 714 guidance and notify applicant promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA eligibility and filing requirements (37 CFR 1.53(d)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application may be filed as a Continued Prosecution Application (CPA) under paragraph (d) provided that: (i) the application is for a design patent; (ii) the prior nonprovisional is a design application complete per §1.51(b) (except possibly inventor's oath/declaration for CPAs filed on/after Sept.16,2012) and contains an application data sheet meeting §1.53(f)(3)(i); and (iii) the CPA is filed before the earliest of payment of the issue fee on the prior application (unless a petition under §1.313(c) is granted), abandonment of the prior application, or termination of proceedings on the prior application. The CPA must identify the prior application and disclose/claim only subject matter disclosed in the prior application; it must name the same inventors (except as provided in (d)(4)), include the request for a CPA, utilize the file jacket and contents of the prior application (including specification, drawings and inventor's oath/declaration), be assigned the application number of the prior application for identification purposes, and be a request to expressly abandon the prior application as of the CPA request filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPA practice is limited to design applications and has precise timing and content requirements. The CPA is intended to utilize the prior application's file and contents; ensure the CPA request includes the identifying information and only claims prior-disclosed subject matter. CPAs carry specific advantages (see guidance) but also strict no-new-matter rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA fees (37 CFR 1.53(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing fee, search fee, and examination fee for a continued prosecution application filed under paragraph (d) are the basic filing fee as set forth in §1.16(b), the search fee as set forth in §1.16(l), and the examination fee as set forth in §1.16(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must pay the standard filing, search, and examination fees applicable to CPAs per the fee schedule in 37 CFR 1.16; ensure fee codes and amounts correspond to CPA filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventorship rules for CPA filings (37 CFR 1.53(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraph (d) may be filed by fewer than all the inventors named in the prior application, provided the CPA request is accompanied by a statement requesting deletion of the name(s) of persons who are not inventors of the invention being claimed in the new application. No person may be named as an inventor in a CPA who was not named as an inventor in the prior application on the date the CPA was filed, except by correction of inventorship under §1.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CPAs cannot add inventors not previously named in the prior file (except via formal correction). To remove inventors, submit the deletion statement with the request. Corrections to inventorship must follow §1.48 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new matter in CPA; substitute specification and amendment handling (37 CFR 1.53(d)(5) and §1.125)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new change must be made as an amendment to the prior application as it existed prior to filing the CPA. No amendment in a CPA may introduce new matter. Any new specification filed with the CPA request will not be considered part of the original application papers but will be treated as a substitute specification in accordance with §1.125. Substitute specifications that include new matter will be denied entry. Preliminary amendments other than substitute specifications will ordinarily be entered, but any new matter entered must be canceled from the descriptive portion of the specification; claims relying upon such new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure substitute specifications assert no new matter and comply with §1.125(b) requirements (including statement that no new matter is included). If new matter is present, expect cancellation/112(a) rejections. Applicants can petition under §1.182 to remove an amendment from CPA and request it be made a separate application (with a new file and filing date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of confidentiality upon CPA filing (37 CFR 1.53(d)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a CPA under paragraph (d) will be construed to include a waiver of confidentiality by the applicant under 35 U.S.C. 122 to the extent that any member of the public entitled under §1.14 to access to, copies of, or information concerning either the prior application or any continuing application filed under this paragraph, may be given similar access to, copies of, or similar information concerning the other application(s) in the file jacket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a CPA may broaden public access across related files; applicants should be aware that confidentiality may be waived to allow similar public access between the prior application and the CPA file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific reference requirement for CPAs (37 CFR 1.53(d)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an application under this paragraph is the specific reference required by 35 U.S.C. 120 to every application assigned the application number identified in such request. No amendment in a CPA may delete this specific reference to any prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to delete the specific reference to the prior application in CPA amendments; that reference is the statutory linkage for benefit/priority and must remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information applicants should furnish with CPA request (37 CFR 1.53(d)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to identifying the application number of the prior application, the applicant should furnish in the request for a CPA the following information relating to the prior application to the best of his or her ability: (i) Title of invention; (ii) Name of applicant(s); and (iii) Correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the listed identifying information in the CPA request to assist USPTO processing and to make the record clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA practice eliminated for utility and plant applications (effective July 14, 2003) and handling of improper CPAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective July 14, 2003, CPA practice was eliminated as to utility and plant applications; applicants who wish to continue examination after prosecution is closed should consider filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114. An improper CPA filed on or after July 14, 2003 in a utility or plant application will not be treated as a CPA; if the utility/plant application has filing date on/after June 8,1995, an improper CPA filed on/after July 14,2003 is treated as a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114. If the requirements of 1.114 are not satisfied, the Office treats the improper CPA as an improper RCE and will send a Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (PTO-2051). For applications filed before June 8,1995, the Office cannot treat an improper CPA as an RCE and will notify applicant of the improper CPA; applicant may file a continuing application under 37 CFR 1.53(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the dates: CPAs eliminated for utility/plant apps after July 14,2003. Improper CPAs in post-June-8-1995 apps may be converted/treated as RCEs (with consequences if RCE requirements lacking). For pre-June-8-1995 apps, CPAs cannot be treated as RCEs; follow MPEP guidance and petitioner/notice procedures. Be aware applicants cannot, as a matter of right, obtain continued examination on claims independent and distinct from previously claimed inventions (cannot 'switch inventions' via RCE) per 37 CFR 1.145.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPA advantages and recommendations for design CPAs (processing and preliminary amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)) for design applications generally requires fewer papers to secure a filing date than a 1.53(b) continuation, the Office will not normally issue a new filing receipt, and the time delay to first Office action should be less. For examination priority purposes, the USPTO will treat continuation CPAs as 'amended' applications (as of the CPA filing date) rather than 'new' applications in certain circumstances. Applicants are strongly encouraged to file any preliminary amendment in a CPA at the time the CPA is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because CPAs may be acted on sooner, filing preliminary amendments at filing can be advantageous. Beware that if no Office action has been issued in the prior application, the CPA may be treated as a 'new' application unless special actions (petition to make special, request for expedited exam) are filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of substitute specifications or preliminary amendments that contain new matter in a CPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Any substitute specification containing new matter filed with a CPA will be denied entry by the substitute specification or preliminary amendment examiner. Preliminary amendments (other than substitute specification) filed with a CPA request will ordinarily be entered, but any new matter which is entered will be required to be canceled from the descriptive portion of the specification. Any claim(s) which relies upon such new matter for support will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(a). An applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 requesting that the amendment be removed from the CPA application file and be accorded status as a separate application (new file and filing date) if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include new matter in substitute specifications for CPAs; if new matter is present, expect denial of entry for substitute spec or cancellation and 112(a) rejections. Petition under §1.182 may be available to seek separate application status for the amendment, but applicants will not automatically receive refunds of fees if petition granted.
